source.text: Ταῦτα ἐλάλησεν Ἰησοῦς, καὶ ἐπάρας τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εἶπεν· Πάτερ, ἐλήλυθεν ἡ ὥρα· δόξασόν σου τὸν υἱόν, ἵνα ὁ υἱὸς δοξάσῃ σέ, καθὼς ἔδωκας αὐτῷ ἐξουσίαν πάσης σαρκός, ἵνα πᾶν ὃ δέδωκας αὐτῷ δώσῃ αὐτοῖς ζωὴν αἰώνιον.

records.literal_gloss: These things spoke Jesus, and having lifted up the eyes of him to the heaven he said, "Father, has come the hour; glorify of you the Son, that the Son may glorify you, \v 2 just as you gave him authority of all flesh, that all that you have given him he may give to them life eternal.

en.L: Jesus spoke these things, and having lifted up {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eyes to heaven, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Father, the hour has come; glorify {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} Son, so that the Son may glorify {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \v 2 just as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} authority over all flesh, so that all that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, to them {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} may give eternal life.
en.B: After Jesus had said these things, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} raised {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eyes toward heaven and prayed: "Father, the hour has come. Glorify {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} Son, so that the Son may glorify {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \v 2 For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} authority over all people, in order that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} may give eternal life to everyone {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: When Jesus had finished saying these things, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} looked up toward heaven and prayed. He said, "Father, the hour has come. Bring glory to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} Son, so that the Son can bring glory to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \v 2 You have put {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in charge of all people. You did this so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} could give eternal life to all the people {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Jesús habló estas cosas, y, alzando {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} ojos al cielo, dijo: «Padre, ha llegado la hora; glorifica a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} Hijo, para que el Hijo {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} glorifique, \v 2 así como {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} diste autoridad sobre toda carne, para que a todo lo que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} has dado, a ellos les dé vida eterna.
es.B: Después de decir estas cosas, Jesús levantó la mirada al cielo y oró: «Padre, ha llegado la hora. Glorifica a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} Hijo, para que el Hijo, a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} vez, {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} glorifique. \v 2 Pues {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} has dado autoridad sobre toda la humanidad, a fin de que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} dé vida eterna a todos los que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} has dado.
es.R: Cuando Jesús terminó de decir estas cosas, miró hacia el cielo y oró así: «Padre, ha llegado la hora. Muestra la gloria de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} Hijo, para que el Hijo muestre {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} gloria. \v 2 Tú {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} diste autoridad sobre toda la gente. Lo hiciste para que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} pudiera dar vida eterna a todos los que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} has dado.

fr.L: Jésus dit ces choses, et, ayant levé {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} yeux vers le ciel, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit : « Père, l’heure est venue ; glorifie {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} Fils, afin que le Fils {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} glorifie, \v 2 selon que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} as donné autorité sur toute chair, afin que tout ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} as donné, à eux {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} donne la vie éternelle.
fr.B: Quand Jésus eut dit ces choses, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leva les yeux vers le ciel et pria : « Père, l’heure est venue. Glorifie {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} Fils, pour que le Fils {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} glorifie. \v 2 Car {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} as donné autorité sur tous les êtres humains, pour qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} donne la vie éternelle à tous ceux que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} as donnés.
fr.R: Quand Jésus a eu fini de dire ces choses, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a levé les yeux vers le ciel et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a prié. Il a dit : « Père, l’heure est venue. Montre la gloire de {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} Fils, pour que le Fils montre {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} gloire. \v 2 Tu {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} as donné autorité sur tous les êtres humains. Tu l’as fait pour qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} puisse donner la vie éternelle à tous ceux que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} as donnés.

sw.L: Yesu alisema mambo haya, na akiinua macho {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kuelekea mbinguni, akasema, "Baba, saa imefika; mtukuze Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, ili Mwana akutukuze {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, \v 2 sawasawa na ulivyompa mamlaka juu ya wote wenye mwili, ili kila kitu ambacho umempa, hao awape uzima wa milele.
sw.B: Yesu alipokwisha kusema mambo haya, aliinua macho {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kuelekea mbinguni, akaomba: "Baba, saa imefika. Mtukuze Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, ili Mwana akutukuze {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}. \v 2 Kwa maana umempa mamlaka juu ya watu wote, ili awape uzima wa milele wote ambao umempa.
sw.R: Yesu alipomaliza kusema mambo haya, alitazama juu mbinguni, akaomba. Akasema, "Baba, saa imefika. Mpe Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} utukufu, ili Mwana naye akupe {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} utukufu. \v 2 Umempa mamlaka juu ya watu wote. Ulifanya hivyo ili awape uzima wa milele watu wote ambao umempa.

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu đã nói những điều này, rồi ngước mắt lên trời, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói: "Lạy Cha, giờ đã đến; xin Cha tôn vinh Con của Cha, để Con tôn vinh Cha, \v 2 như Cha đã ban cho Con quyền trên mọi xác thịt, để tất cả những gì Cha đã ban cho Con, Con ban cho họ sự sống đời đời.
vi.B: Sau khi nói những điều này, Đức Giê-xu ngước mắt lên trời và cầu nguyện: "Lạy Cha, giờ đã đến. Xin Cha tôn vinh Con của Cha, để Con tôn vinh Cha. \v 2 Vì Cha đã ban cho Con quyền trên mọi người, để Con ban sự sống đời đời cho tất cả những người Cha đã giao cho Con.
vi.R: Khi Đức Giê-xu nói xong những điều này, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ngước nhìn lên trời và cầu nguyện. Ngài nói: "Lạy Cha, giờ đã đến. Xin Cha tôn vinh Con của Cha, để Con cũng tôn vinh Cha. \v 2 Cha đã giao cho Con quyền trên mọi người. Cha làm vậy để Con ban sự sống đời đời cho tất cả những người Cha đã giao cho Con.

ko.L: 예수께서 이것들을 말씀하시고, 눈을 들어 하늘을 우러러보시며 말씀하셨다. "아버지, 때가 왔습니다. 아버지의 아들을 영광스럽게 하셔서, 아들이 아버지를 영광스럽게 하게 하십시오. \v 2 아버지께서 아들에게 모든 육체를 다스리는 권세를 주신 것처럼, 아버지께서 아들에게 주신 모든 것, 곧 그들에게 아들이 영원한 생명을 주게 하시려는 것입니다.
ko.B: 예수께서 이 말씀을 하신 뒤에 눈을 들어 하늘을 우러러보시며 기도하셨다. "아버지, 때가 되었습니다. 아버지의 아들을 영광스럽게 하셔서, 아들이 아버지를 영광스럽게 하게 해 주십시오. \v 2 아버지께서는 아들에게 모든 사람을 다스리는 권세를 주셨습니다. 그것은 아버지께서 아들에게 주신 모든 사람에게 아들이 영원한 생명을 주게 하시려는 것입니다.
ko.R: 예수께서 이 말씀을 마치시고 하늘을 쳐다보시며 기도하셨다. "아버지, 때가 되었습니다. 아버지의 아들이 영광을 받게 해 주십시오. 그래서 아들이 아버지께 영광을 돌리게 해 주십시오. \v 2 아버지께서는 아들에게 모든 사람을 맡기셨습니다. 아버지께서 아들에게 주신 모든 사람에게 아들이 영원한 생명을 주게 하시려고 그렇게 하셨습니다.

pt.L: Jesus falou estas coisas e, levantando os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} olhos para o céu, disse: "Pai, chegou a hora; glorifica o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} Filho, para que o Filho {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} glorifique, \v 2 assim como {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} deste autoridade sobre toda carne, para que, a tudo o que {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} deste, a eles {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} dê a vida eterna.
pt.B: Depois de dizer essas coisas, Jesus ergueu os olhos para o céu e orou: "Pai, chegou a hora. Glorifica o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} Filho, para que o Filho {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} glorifique. \v 2 Pois {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} deste autoridade sobre todas as pessoas, para que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} dê a vida eterna a todos os que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} deste.
pt.R: Quando Jesus terminou de dizer essas coisas, olhou para o céu e orou. Ele disse: "Pai, chegou a hora. Dá glória ao {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} Filho, para que o Filho possa dar glória a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}. \v 2 Tu {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} deste poder sobre todas as pessoas. Fizeste isso para que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} pudesse dar a vida eterna a todas as pessoas que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} deste.

am.L: ኢየሱስ ይህን ተናገረ፤ ዓይኖቹንም ወደ ሰማይ አንሥቶ እንዲህ አለ፦ «አባት ሆይ፣ ሰዓቱ መጥቷል፤ ልጅህን አክብረው፤ ልጁም አንተን እንዲያከብርህ፤ \v 2 በሥጋ ሁሉ ላይ ሥልጣን እንደ ሰጠኸው፣ የሰጠኸውን ሁሉ፣ ለእነርሱ የዘላለም ሕይወትን እንዲሰጣቸው።
am.B: ኢየሱስ ይህን ከተናገረ በኋላ ዓይኖቹን ወደ ሰማይ አንሥቶ እንዲህ ብሎ ጸለየ፦ «አባት ሆይ፣ ሰዓቱ ደርሷል። ልጁ አንተን እንዲያከብርህ ልጅህን አክብረው። \v 2 ለሰጠኸው ሁሉ የዘላለም ሕይወትን እንዲሰጥ በሰው ሁሉ ላይ ሥልጣን ሰጥተኸዋልና።
am.R: ኢየሱስ ይህን ተናግሮ ከጨረሰ በኋላ ወደ ሰማይ ተመልክቶ ጸለየ። እንዲህም አለ፦ «አባት ሆይ፣ ሰዓቱ ደርሷል። ልጅህ አንተን እንዲያከብርህ ልጅህን አክብረው። \v 2 በሰዎች ሁሉ ላይ ሥልጣን ሰጥተኸዋል። ይህን ያደረግኸው ለሰጠኸው ሰዎች ሁሉ የዘላለም ሕይወት እንዲሰጣቸው ነው።

decisions.choice: the hour: the appointed time of Jesus's death and glorification, which has now arrived
alternatives: a period of time in general
decisions.reason: Through the Gospel Jesus's hour had not yet come (2:4; 7:30; 8:20). At 12:23 he said that it had come, and at 13:1 John calls it the hour to pass from this world to the Father. Here, at the start of his prayer, Jesus says it again to the Father: the cross, resurrection and return to the Father are at hand.

decisions.choice: glorify your Son so that the Son may glorify you: the Father shows the Son's glory in the hour, and in that same event the Son shows the Father's
decisions.reason: Glorify is a key term. In John, Jesus is glorified when he is lifted up on the cross, raised, and returns to the Father (7:39; 12:23; 13:31-32). The glory of the two is bound together: when the Son is glorified, so is the Father (13:31-32; 14:13). Jesus's first request is not for his own sake alone but so that the Father may be honored.

decisions.choice: so that the Son may glorify you (SBLGNT)
alternatives: so that your Son also may glorify you (many later manuscripts)
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "so that your Son also may glorify you", adding "also" and "your", which repeats the wording of the first request. The older manuscripts, among them Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus, have the shorter text. The meaning is the same either way. A footnote gives the longer reading. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: authority over all flesh: authority over all human beings
decisions.reason: "All flesh" is a Hebrew way of speaking of all humankind, or of all living things (Genesis 6:12; Isaiah 40:5; Joel 2:28). Here the purpose clause that follows shows that people are meant: the authority is given so that the Son may give life. Compare the authority given to the Son to judge (5:27) and the Father giving all things into his hand (3:35).

decisions.choice: all that you have given him ... to them: the people given to the Son, seen first as one whole and then as persons
alternatives: all things that you have given him (things, not people)
decisions.reason: πᾶν ὃ is neuter, "all that": John speaks of all whom the Father gives as a single gift, as in 6:37 and 6:39. The sentence then turns to the plural masculine "to them", the persons who make up that gift. The neuter phrase stands first for emphasis and is taken up by "to them".

decisions.choice: just as: the gift of authority is the ground of the request
decisions.reason: καθὼς can compare ("just as") or give a reason ("since"). Here it does both: the Son asks to be glorified in keeping with what the Father has already given him, authority over all people, which has eternal life as its purpose.

decisions.choice: you, your, yours, yourself (to the Father); he, him, his, me, my (of the Son); in the whole prayer
decisions.reason: In this prayer Jesus speaks to the Father, so every "you" and "your" addressed to him uses the deity_pronoun setting, and so does every "me" and "my" with which Jesus speaks of himself and every "he" or "him" for the Son, as in 11:41-42. Plain "You" and "He" stand at the start of a sentence. The prayer runs to 17:26, so the quotation opened here does not close in this passage.

decisions.choice: all flesh, all that (L); all people, everyone (B); all people, all the people (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the idiom and the neuter. Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means (meaning decision m4) and use words for people where the Greek neuter means people (meaning decision m5), as 6:37 does. "All people" and "everyone" are already inclusive, so they need no gender setting.

decisions.choice: prayed (B, R); Bring glory to; put him in charge of; You did this so that
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly that what follows is a prayer, says "bring glory to" (as at 12:28), which keeps the key term in everyday speech, and splits the long sentence. "Hour" stays at every level, as at 12:23, so the thread through the Gospel stays visible.

decisions.choice: pretérito at every level (habló, dijo; oró)
decisions.reason: Here John tells the event in past tenses, so every level uses the pretérito; where he uses the historic present elsewhere, Literal keeps it and Balanced and Readable use the pretérito. Balanced and Readable say "oró", since what follows is a prayer.

decisions.choice: every pronoun for the Father or the Son, in the whole prayer
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to the Father with "tú", as in 11:41-42. By the book-wide rule (1:1), every pronoun for the Father or the Son takes the deity pronoun setting: stressed (tú, ti, él, mí), possessive (tu, mi, mía, su, sus) and object pronouns before the verb (te, le, me). A pronoun at the start of a sentence ("Tú", "Lo") is written plain, as are pronouns joined to the verb ("glorifícame", "conocerte") and "contigo".

decisions.choice: toda carne, todo lo que (L); toda la humanidad, todos los que (B); toda la gente, todos los que (R); muestra la gloria (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the idiom and the neuter; Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means (meaning decision m4) and use words for people where the neuter means people (meaning decision m5), as at 6:37. These words are already inclusive and need no gender setting. Readable says "mostrar la gloria", as at 12:28. "Hora" stays at every level.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B; "dit", "leva", "pria"); passé composé (R; "a levé", "a prié"); the prayer in the passé composé at every level ("je t’ai glorifié", "tu m’as donné")
alternatives: passé composé for narration at every level
decisions.reason: The French brief for the passage (17:1-8), as in 1:19. The narration is only the opening clause; the rest is Jesus's prayer, where every level uses the passé composé for the Greek past tenses, as people speak.

decisions.choice: tu to the Father, with {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}}, {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}}, {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}, {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}}, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}}; the Son's pronouns ({{deity_pronoun:il|Il}}, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}}) also under the setting, through the whole prayer
decisions.reason: The French brief: God is addressed with "tu", as in the Lord's Prayer in French since 1966 and in every modern French Bible; "vous" would add a distance the Greek does not have. Every pronoun for the Father and for the Son takes the deity_pronoun setting, as the English does (r-en-1); a pronoun that begins a sentence ("Tu lui as donné") is written plainly with its capital.

decisions.choice: Montre la gloire de ton Fils, pour que le Fils montre ta gloire (R); glorifier (L, B)
decisions.reason: "Glorifier" is the book-wide word and is kept at Literal and Balanced. For young readers it is church language, so Readable says what the request means (meaning decision m2): the Father shows the Son's glory and the Son shows the Father's. The key word "gloire" stays; verses 4-5 do the same.

decisions.choice: the past at every level (alisema, akasema); Balanced and Readable "akaomba" (prayed)
decisions.reason: The Greek verbs here are past tenses, so Literal tells in the past too; Balanced uses "-li-" and then "-ka-", as written Swahili narrative does, and Readable the plain past. Balanced and Readable say "akaomba", as the English says "prayed".

decisions.choice: the Father addressed with "wewe"; spans on wewe, nawe, wako, lako, yako, kwako, and on the Son's mimi, -angu
decisions.reason: In this prayer Jesus speaks to the Father, whom Swahili addresses with "wewe" (style guide, section 6). The free pronouns and possessives for the Father and for the Son carry the reader setting; the subject and object prefixes ("akutukuze", "umempa") cannot, so Swahili has far fewer spans than the English. One at the start of a sentence is written plain. This holds for the whole prayer.

decisions.choice: wote wenye mwili, kila kitu ambacho umempa (L); watu wote, wote ambao umempa (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the idiom "all flesh" and the neuter "all that", as Literal does at 6:37 and 6:39; Balanced and Readable say what both mean, people (meaning notes m4, m5). "Watu" is already inclusive, so there is no gender span. Readable says "mpe ... utukufu" for glorify, as at 12:28.

decisions.choice: "Cha" for the Father and "Con" for Jesus himself, with no setting spans, through the whole prayer
decisions.reason: As the style guide sets for John 17, Jesus speaks to the Father as a son to his father: he says "Cha" where the Greek has "you" and "Con" for "I", "me" and "the Son". Both are capitalised nouns and take no deity_pronoun setting, where the English has one on every pronoun.

decisions.choice: nói (L); cầu nguyện (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal introduces the prayer with the book's plain verb for Jesus speaking; Balanced and Readable say what the words are, a prayer, as the English does.

decisions.choice: Jesus prays in the formal polite style (합쇼체), calls himself 저 (아들 in the third person, without the honorific), and addresses the Father by title (아버지, 아버지께서) rather than with a pronoun
decisions.reason: The guide gives Jesus 합쇼체 when he speaks to the Father (style guide section 4), as in 12:27-28; Korean addresses a superior by title, and 당신 would be cold or odd in prayer. This holds for the whole prayer (17:1-26).

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean
alternatives: capitalised pronoun spans as in English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change; respect is carried by the honorific -si-, 께서 and 그분 at every level (style guide section 7).

decisions.choice: 모든 육체 (L); 모든 사람 (B, R) for "all flesh"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew idiom; Balanced and Readable say what it means.

decisions.choice: tu, te, ti, teu, tua, contigo to the Father throughout the prayer, each under the deity_pronoun setting
alternatives: o Senhor (as a pronoun of address)
decisions.reason: Jesus prays to the Father, and anyone who speaks to God uses "tu" with the verb in the second person singular ("glorifica", "deste", "enviaste"), the living form of prayer in Brazil (style section 4). Every "tu", "te", "ti", "teu", "tua" and "contigo" for the Father takes the deity_pronoun setting, as the English "you" and "your" do; so do "me", "mim", "meu" when Jesus speaks of himself, and "ele", "o", "lhe" for the Son. Where Portuguese leaves the subject unstated, there is no pronoun to mark.

decisions.choice: Dá glória ao teu Filho ... dar glória a ti
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the key word "glória" in an everyday phrase, as the English Readable says "bring glory to"; Literal and Balanced say "glorificar".

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in the Amharic
alternatives: Marking pronouns for God and Jesus in some other way
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting that capitalises pronouns for God and Jesus in English has nothing to change in Amharic; most such pronouns are verb suffixes in any case.

decisions.choice: "አባት ሆይ" (Father) and the familiar "አንተ" (you) through the whole prayer
decisions.reason: As in the Bible tradition and in prayer, God is addressed with "አንተ"; the respect lies in the words, not the pronoun. John's Greek has the plain vocative "Father" here and in 17:5, 11, 21, 24 and 25, so Amharic says "አባት ሆይ" rather than "my Father".

source.text: αὕτη δέ ἐστιν ἡ αἰώνιος ζωὴ ἵνα γινώσκωσι σὲ τὸν μόνον ἀληθινὸν θεὸν καὶ ὃν ἀπέστειλας Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν.

records.literal_gloss: This and is the eternal life, that they may know you the only true God and whom you sent, Jesus Christ.

en.L: And this is eternal life, that they may know {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, the only true God, and [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} sent, Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: And eternal life is this: that they know {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, the only true God, and the one {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} sent, Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: Eternal life means knowing {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, the only true God. It means knowing the one {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} sent, Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

es.L: Y esta es la vida eterna: que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} conozcan a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, el solo Dios verdadero, y a quien enviaste, {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús Mesías}}.
es.B: Y esta es la vida eterna: que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} conozcan a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, que eres el único Dios verdadero, y al que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} enviaste, {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.
es.R: La vida eterna es conocerte a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, el único Dios verdadero. Es también conocer al que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} enviaste, {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.

fr.L: Or ceci est la vie éternelle : qu’ils {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} connaissent, {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, le seul vrai Dieu, et [celui] que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as envoyé, Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.B: Et la vie éternelle, la voici : qu’ils {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} connaissent, {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, le seul vrai Dieu, ainsi que celui que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as envoyé, Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}.
fr.R: La vie éternelle, c’est {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} connaître, {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, le seul vrai Dieu. C’est aussi connaître celui que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as envoyé, Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}.

sw.L: Na huu ndio uzima wa milele, kwamba wakujue {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, Mungu pekee aliye wa kweli, na [yule] uliyemtuma, Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.B: Na uzima wa milele ni huu: kwamba wakujue {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, Mungu pekee aliye wa kweli, na yule uliyemtuma, Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.R: Uzima wa milele ni kukujua {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, Mungu pekee wa kweli. Ni kumjua pia yule uliyemtuma, Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.

vi.L: Và đây là sự sống đời đời: là họ biết Cha, Đức Chúa Trời thật duy nhất, và [Đấng] Cha đã sai, Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}.
vi.B: Và sự sống đời đời là đây: được biết Cha, Đức Chúa Trời thật và duy nhất, và biết Đấng Cha đã sai đến, là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}.
vi.R: Sự sống đời đời là được biết Cha, là Đức Chúa Trời thật duy nhất. Đó cũng là được biết Đấng Cha đã sai đến, là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}.

ko.L: 영원한 생명은 이것입니다. 곧 그들이 유일하신 참 하나님이신 아버지와, 아버지께서 보내신 [이] 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 아는 것입니다.
ko.B: 영원한 생명은 이것입니다. 그들이 오직 한 분이신 참 하나님 아버지와, 아버지께서 보내신 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 아는 것입니다.
ko.R: 영원한 생명이란, 오직 한 분이신 참 하나님, 곧 아버지를 아는 것입니다. 또 아버지께서 보내신 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 아는 것입니다.

pt.L: E esta é a vida eterna: que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} conheçam, a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, o único Deus verdadeiro, e [aquele] a quem enviaste, Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}}.
pt.B: E a vida eterna é esta: que conheçam a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, o único Deus verdadeiro, e aquele que enviaste, Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}}.
pt.R: A vida eterna é conhecer a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, o único Deus verdadeiro. É conhecer aquele que enviaste, Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}}.

am.L: የዘላለም ሕይወትም ይህ ነው፤ ብቸኛ እውነተኛ አምላክ የሆንከውን አንተን፣ የላክኸውንም ኢየሱስ {{christos:ክርስቶስን|መሲሕን}} እንዲያውቁ።
am.B: የዘላለም ሕይወት ይህ ነው፤ ብቸኛውን እውነተኛ አምላክ አንተን፣ የላክኸውንም ኢየሱስ {{christos:ክርስቶስን|መሲሕን}} ማወቅ።
am.R: የዘላለም ሕይወት ማለት ብቸኛ እውነተኛ አምላክ የሆንከውን አንተን ማወቅ ነው። የላክኸውን ኢየሱስ {{christos:ክርስቶስን|መሲሕን}} ማወቅም ነው።

decisions.choice: this is eternal life, that: the clause says what eternal life is
alternatives: this leads to eternal life, that they know
decisions.reason: "This" points forward to the clause that follows, which explains it, as in 6:29, 6:40 and 15:12. Eternal life is not only something that knowing God leads to; knowing God is what it consists of. Verse 2 spoke of the Son giving eternal life; this verse says what that life is.

decisions.choice: know: an ongoing, personal knowing, the knowing of a relationship
decisions.reason: γινώσκωσι is present tense: knowing that goes on, not a single act of learning. In the Bible to know God is to be in a living relationship with him, not only to know facts about him (Jeremiah 31:34; Hosea 6:6). Jesus speaks of the shepherd and the sheep knowing each other, as he and the Father know each other (10:14-15).

decisions.choice: the only true God, and the one he sent: the one God, known together with the Son he sent
decisions.reason: "The only true God" holds to the confession of Israel that there is one God (Deuteronomy 6:4; compare 5:44). Beside him stands the one he sent, and knowing the Son belongs to the same eternal life. John keeps both truths together: there is one God, and the Son is with God and is God (1:1, 18; 10:30).

decisions.choice: Jesus Christ: Jesus names himself in the third person, with the full name, in the prayer
alternatives: Jesus's own words, a solemn naming of himself
John's own wording of the prayer
decisions.reason: The full name "Jesus Christ" occurs in this Gospel only here and at 1:17, and nowhere else does Jesus use it of himself. It is the way believers spoke of him after the resurrection. It may be that John, in giving the prayer, puts it in the words the church used, or Jesus may speak of himself in this solemn way as the one the Father sent. The text does not settle which. Christ is a title, "anointed one" (1:41).

decisions.choice: Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: As at 1:17, the title follows the name with the christos setting. The name stays at the end, as in the Greek, so the sentence closes on it.

decisions.choice: Eternal life means knowing ... It means knowing
decisions.reason: Readable uses "knowing" to show that the knowing goes on (meaning decision m2), and says it twice so the reader sees that the Son is known together with the Father (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús Mesías}} (L); {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: As at 1:17: Spanish writes name and title as one word, so the span takes in the name. The name stays at the end, as in the Greek. Literal says "el solo Dios verdadero" for "the only true God", word for word.

decisions.choice: es conocerte ... Es también conocer
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable says "conocer" twice so the reader sees that the knowing goes on (meaning decision m2) and that the Son is known together with the Father (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}} (L); Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the style guide asks: no hyphen, so that both options read naturally. Literal follows the English Literal, which has no article; Balanced and Readable add "le" to the alternative so that it reads as a title (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, at the end of the sentence
decisions.reason: As at 1:17: Swahili has no article, so "Yesu Masihi" reads as naturally as "Yesu Kristo" at every level. The name stays at the end, as in the Greek. "Wa kweli" (true) is the same word as the key term for truth.

decisions.choice: Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}} at every level
decisions.reason: The style guide's form for the title with the name. Vietnamese needs no article, so the same span serves all three levels.

decisions.choice: Đức Chúa Trời thật
decisions.reason: The guide keeps "chân lý" for the noun "truth" and uses "thật" for the adjective "true", as in "ánh sáng thật".

decisions.choice: 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} at every level
alternatives: the English article ("the Messiah") at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: Korean has no article, so one span serves every level (style guide section 7).

decisions.choice: [이] for "the one" whom the Father sent
decisions.reason: Korean needs a noun for the relative clause; Jesus speaking of himself does not call himself 분, so the plain 이 is supplied in brackets.

decisions.choice: Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}} at every level
decisions.reason: The English Literal has "Messiah" without the article. In Portuguese "Jesus Messias" reads like a double name, so every level writes "o Messias" in the alternative (style section 7).

decisions.choice: "ብቸኛ እውነተኛ አምላክ" (the only true God), with "አምላክ"
decisions.reason: Here "God" describes the one addressed ("you, the only true God"), so Amharic uses "አምላክ", the word for God as a description, as it does for a predicate; "እግዚአብሔር" is a name and does not take "the only true" naturally. The accusative ending goes inside each option of the christos span ("ክርስቶስን", "መሲሕን").

source.text: ἐγώ σε ἐδόξασα ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, τὸ ἔργον τελειώσας ὃ δέδωκάς μοι ἵνα ποιήσω·

records.literal_gloss: I you glorified on the earth, the work having completed that you have given me that I should do.

en.L: I glorified {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} on the earth, having completed the work which {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to do.
en.B: I have glorified {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} on earth by completing the work that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to do.
en.R: I have brought glory to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} here on earth. I have finished the work {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to do.

es.L: Yo {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} glorifiqué en la tierra, habiendo llevado a término la obra que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} has dado para que haga.
es.B: Yo {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} he glorificado en la tierra llevando a cabo la obra que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} encargaste.
es.R: Yo he mostrado {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} gloria aquí en la tierra. He terminado el trabajo que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} encargaste.

fr.L: Moi, je {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}ai glorifié sur la terre, ayant achevé l’œuvre que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as donnée à faire.
fr.B: Je {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}ai glorifié sur la terre en achevant l’œuvre que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as confiée.
fr.R: J’ai montré {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} gloire ici, sur la terre. J’ai terminé le travail que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}avais donné à faire.

sw.L: Mimi nilikutukuza duniani, nikiwa nimeikamilisha kazi ambayo umenipa niifanye.
sw.B: Nimekutukuza duniani kwa kuikamilisha kazi uliyonipa niifanye.
sw.R: Nimekupa utukufu hapa duniani. Nimeimaliza kazi uliyonipa niifanye.

vi.L: Con đã tôn vinh Cha trên đất, khi đã hoàn tất công việc Cha đã giao cho Con làm.
vi.B: Con đã tôn vinh Cha trên đất bằng cách hoàn tất công việc Cha giao cho Con làm.
vi.R: Con đã tôn vinh Cha ở dưới đất này. Con đã làm xong công việc Cha giao cho Con.

ko.L: 저는 땅에서 아버지를 영광스럽게 하였으니, 아버지께서 저에게 하라고 주신 일을 다 이루었습니다.
ko.B: 저는 아버지께서 저에게 하라고 맡기신 일을 다 이루어서, 땅에서 아버지를 영광스럽게 하였습니다.
ko.R: 저는 이 땅에서 아버지께 영광을 돌렸습니다. 아버지께서 저에게 맡기신 일을 다 마쳤습니다.

pt.L: Eu {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} glorifiquei na terra, tendo completado a obra que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} deste para fazer.
pt.B: Eu {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} glorifiquei na terra, completando a obra que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} deste para fazer.
pt.R: Eu {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} dei glória aqui na terra. Eu terminei o trabalho que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} deste para fazer.

am.L: እኔ በምድር ላይ አከበርኩህ፤ እንዳደርገው የሰጠኸኝን ሥራ ፈጽሜ።
am.B: እንድሠራው የሰጠኸኝን ሥራ በመፈጸም በምድር ላይ አክብሬሃለሁ።
am.R: እዚህ በምድር ላይ አክብሬሃለሁ። እንድሠራው የሰጠኸኝን ሥራ ጨርሻለሁ።

decisions.choice: Jesus glorified the Father by doing the work the Father gave him
decisions.reason: Jesus's whole life has shown who the Father is: his signs revealed God's glory (2:11; 11:4, 40), and his words were the Father's (12:49-50). He has said from the start that his food is to do the will of the one who sent him and to finish his work (4:34), and that his works bear witness that the Father sent him (5:36). The "I" is emphatic: this is what the Son has done; verse 5 asks what the Father will do.

decisions.choice: having completed: the work is spoken of as done, though the cross is still ahead
alternatives: the work of teaching only, apart from the cross
decisions.reason: τελειώσας is an aorist participle: the Son has brought the work to its goal. As in 13:31, Jesus speaks from the hour itself, so the cross that completes the work is counted with it. "On earth" sets this beside verse 5, where he asks for glory in the Father's presence.

decisions.choice: a link with Jesus's last word on the cross, "It is finished" (19:30)
decisions.reason: On the cross Jesus says Τετέλεσται (19:30), a closely related verb, and John uses this verb for the completing of Scripture just before (19:28). The work he says here is complete is the one he declares finished there. John does not mark the link, so it is noted as likely, not certain.

decisions.choice: have glorified ... by completing (B); have brought glory to ... I have finished (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced shows by "by" how the Father was glorified (meaning decision m1). Readable says "brought glory to" as elsewhere in the prayer and makes the two parts two sentences.

decisions.choice: te he glorificado ... llevando a cabo (B); he mostrado tu gloria ... He terminado (R); me encargaste (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Balanced shows how the Father was glorified (meaning decision m1), and Readable makes two sentences. "Encargar" is the everyday Spanish for giving someone a work to do. "Yo" keeps the emphatic "I".

decisions.choice: kuikamilisha kazi (L, B); kuimaliza kazi (R)
decisions.reason: The same words as 4:34 at each level, where Jesus says that his food is to finish the Father's work. The emphatic "I" opens the Literal sentence and is written plain.

decisions.choice: 다 이루다 for "having completed"
decisions.reason: 다 이루다 is the natural Korean for finishing a task given, and lets readers hear the link with Jesus's last word in 19:30.

decisions.choice: "አከበረ" (glorify) and "ክብር" (glory) at every level
decisions.reason: Glory and glorify are key terms in John and are one word family in Greek; "ክብር" and "አከበረ" keep them one family in Amharic, so 17:1, 4, 5, 10, 22 and 24 read as one thread. Readable needs no paraphrase such as the English "bring glory to".

source.text: καὶ νῦν δόξασόν με σύ, πάτερ, παρὰ σεαυτῷ τῇ δόξῃ ᾗ εἶχον πρὸ τοῦ τὸν κόσμον εἶναι παρὰ σοί.

records.literal_gloss: And now glorify me you, Father, with yourself with the glory which I was having before the the world to be with you.

en.L: And now, Father, glorify {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}}, with the glory which I had with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} before the world existed.
en.B: So now, Father, glorify {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}}, at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} side, with the glory that was {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}} with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} before there was a world.
en.R: So now, Father, bring glory to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} side. Give {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} the glory I had with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} before the world began.

es.L: Y ahora glorifícame {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}, Padre, junto a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} mismo, con la gloria que tenía, antes de que el mundo existiera, junto a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}.

decisions.choice: glorify me with yourself: in the Father's own presence, by the Father himself
alternatives: in your sight, in your judgment
decisions.reason: "And now" turns from what the Son has done on earth (verse 4) to what he asks the Father to do. The "you" is emphatic: the Father himself is to glorify him. "With yourself" means beside the Father, in his presence, set against "on earth" in verse 4. Jesus is asking to return to where he came from (13:3; 16:28).

decisions.choice: the glory I had with you before the world existed: the Son shared the Father's glory before creation
alternatives: the glory planned for him before the world, not yet his
decisions.reason: The Son speaks of a glory he had with the Father before the world existed, which fits what John says at the start: in the beginning the Word was with God and was God (1:1-2), and all things came into being through him (1:3). The imperfect "I had" describes a lasting state. In Isaiah God says that he gives his glory to no other (Isaiah 42:8), yet the Son had this glory with him. The verse asks for that glory now, in the Father's presence; it does not say that the Son ever stopped being who he was. Compare 17:24.

decisions.choice: the world: the created order
decisions.reason: Here the world is the whole creation, as in 1:10a and 17:24: the glory was there before anything was made.

decisions.choice: yourself, at your side, was mine (B); at your side, Give me the glory I had (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced shows the emphatic "you" with "yourself" and says "at your side" for the Father's presence (meaning decision m1). Readable splits the request and says "before the world began", plainer than "existed"; Balanced says "before there was a world".

decisions.choice: glorifícame tú (L, B); junto a ti mismo (L); a tu lado (B, R); antes de que hubiera mundo (B); antes de que el mundo comenzara (R)
decisions.reason: "Tú" shows the emphatic "you", and "a tu lado" says what "with yourself" means: in the Father's own presence (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the Greek order, with "junto a ti" at the end. "Contigo" has no capital form and takes no setting.

decisions.choice: auprès de toi-même (L); toi-même à tes côtés (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek means both "in your presence" and "by you yourself" (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps "auprès de toi-même"; Balanced says both, as the English does, with "toi-même" and "à tes côtés".

decisions.choice: mbele yako mwenyewe (L); kando yako (B, R)
decisions.reason: "With yourself" means in the Father's own presence, set against "on earth" in verse 4 (meaning note m1). Literal says "mbele yako mwenyewe" (before you yourself); Balanced and Readable say "kando yako" (at your side), as the English does.

decisions.choice: 아버지 곁에서 for "with yourself" and "with you"
decisions.reason: 곁에서 says "in your own presence", the sense of the Greek preposition with the dative; 친히 carries the emphatic "you".

decisions.choice: your name: the Father himself, as he has made himself known
alternatives: a particular new name for God
decisions.reason: In the Bible a name stands for the person as he has shown himself to be. God made his name known to Moses at the bush (Exodus 3:14-15) and proclaimed it on the mountain, as the God who is merciful and gracious, rich in steadfast love and faithfulness (Exodus 34:5-7). Jesus has made the Father known in the same way: whoever has seen him has seen the Father (1:18; 14:9). Compare 12:28 and 17:26.

decisions.choice: revealed: made visible, brought into the open
decisions.reason: Ἐφανέρωσά means to make visible what was hidden. John uses it of Jesus being revealed to Israel (1:31) and of his glory shown in his signs (2:11). The Father has been shown in what Jesus has said and done.

decisions.choice: whom you gave me out of the world: the disciples, given by the Father and taken from the world
decisions.reason: The people meant are first of all the disciples with Jesus that night. They are the Father's gift to him (6:37, 39; 10:29), and they are taken "out of" the world, the mass of humanity that does not know God (15:19; 17:14-16), while they still live in it (17:11, 15).

decisions.choice: the people: human beings, not men in contrast with women
decisions.reason: The word means human beings. Though the disciples at the table are men, the gift of the Father is spoken of in general terms, and the prayer reaches out to all who will believe (17:20).

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The inclusive "people" is the default and "men" the alternative (meaning decision m4), as at 1:4 and 3:19.

decisions.choice: shown who you are
decisions.reason: Readable says what making the Father's name known means (meaning decision m1), since "your name" alone may sound like only a word.

decisions.choice: {{gender:los seres humanos|los hombres}} (L); {{gender:las personas|los hombres}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word means human beings (meaning decision m4): inclusive default, traditional "los hombres" as the alternative, as at 1:4 and 3:19.

decisions.choice: He mostrado quién eres tú
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable says what making the Father's name known means (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: aux {{gender:humains|hommes}} (L, B); aux {{gender:gens|hommes}} (R)
decisions.reason: The word means human beings, not men as against women (meaning decision m4). "Humains" and "gens" are masculine plurals, so "donnés" agrees with either option; "personnes" would need "données" and could not share a span with "hommes". Readable uses the everyday "gens".

decisions.choice: kudhihirisha (L), kujulisha (B); watu, with no gender span
decisions.reason: Literal says "kudhihirisha" (make visible) for the verb's sense (meaning note m2); Balanced says "made known". "Watu" (people) already includes men and women, so, as at 1:4, Swahili has no gender span where the English offers "men" (m4). Readable says what making the name known means (m1).

decisions.choice: những người, with no gender span
alternatives: a gender setting as in the English
decisions.reason: "Người" means a human being of either sex, so the Vietnamese already says what the English gender setting offers; the guide keeps gender spans for "anh chị em".

decisions.choice: 사람들, with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in the English
decisions.reason: Korean 사람들 already means people of either sex; the gender setting has nothing to change (style guide section 7).

decisions.choice: No gender span: "ሰዎች" (people)
decisions.reason: "ሰዎች" already means people, men and women, so Amharic has no second wording for the gender setting to offer; "ወንዶች" (males) would say something the Greek does not.

decisions.choice: they were yours, and you gave them to me: they belonged to the Father before they came to Jesus
decisions.reason: The disciples did not first belong to Jesus and then to God; they were the Father's, and he gave them to the Son (6:37, 44, 65; 10:29). "To me" is emphatic, joined to "and" in one word. The text says that they were the Father's but not how; it does not explain it further.

decisions.choice: kept: held fast to and obeyed
decisions.reason: To keep a word is to hold on to it and do what it says (8:51; 14:23; 15:20). The perfect tense says they have kept it and still do. The disciples will fail Jesus that very night (16:32), but Jesus speaks of their faith as a whole.

decisions.choice: your word: the Father's message, which Jesus spoke
decisions.reason: The word the disciples kept is the Father's, given through Jesus: the word they hear from Jesus is not his own but the Father's who sent him (14:24). Verse 8 speaks of the same thing in the plural, "the words".

decisions.choice: belonged to you (B); obeyed (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced says "belonged to" for the plain "were yours". Readable says "obeyed", the everyday sense of keeping a word (meaning decision m2), so that "kept your word" is not read as keeping a promise.

decisions.choice: a mí me los diste (L); te pertenecían (B); obedecido (R)
decisions.reason: Literal shows the emphatic "to me" (meaning decision m1) and keeps the Greek order of the last clause. Balanced says "te pertenecían" for the plain "were yours"; Readable says "obedecer", the everyday sense of keeping a word (meaning decision m2). "Tuyos" (Literal) and "Te" (Balanced) open the sentence and are written plain; the other pronouns for the Father and the Son take the setting (1:1).

decisions.choice: ta parole
decisions.reason: Here the noun means the Father's message, which Jesus spoke (meaning decision m3), not the title of 1:1, so French uses the ordinary "parole"; "le Verbe" is kept for the title alone.

decisions.choice: they have known (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: Most manuscripts read "they have known". A few read "I have known", and a few have other forms of the verb. "They" fits the flow of the prayer, which in verses 6-8 is all about what the disciples have received and believed. A footnote gives the other reading. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: now they have come to know: a knowing reached and still held
decisions.reason: ἔγνωκαν is perfect tense: they have come to know and now know. "Now" looks back to the last words of the disciples at the supper: "Now we know ... we believe that you came from God" (16:30).

decisions.choice: all you have given me: everything Jesus has, his words and his works, comes from the Father
decisions.reason: What the disciples have come to see is that nothing in Jesus is his own apart from the Father: his words (verse 8; 12:49), his works (5:36), and his authority (17:2). That is the knowing that leads to the faith of verse 8.

decisions.choice: have come to know (B); understand (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced shows the perfect tense, knowing reached and still held (meaning decision m2). Readable says "understand", the everyday word for knowing of this kind.

decisions.choice: han llegado a saber (B); entienden (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Balanced shows the perfect tense, knowing reached and still held (meaning decision m2); Readable says "entender", the everyday word for knowing of this kind.

decisions.choice: for: this explains how the disciples came to know (verse 7)
decisions.reason: ὅτι here gives the reason for verse 7: they know that everything Jesus has comes from the Father because he gave them the Father's words, and they received them.

decisions.choice: the words: the sayings Jesus spoke, all of which came from the Father
decisions.reason: The plural ῥήματα means the things Jesus said one by one; the singular "word" in verse 6 is the message as a whole. Jesus has said that he speaks only what the Father told him (12:49-50; 14:10). John uses the plural for the words that give life (6:63, 68).

decisions.choice: knew truly: came to know with real certainty
decisions.reason: ἀληθῶς means "truly" or "in truth": their knowing is real and sure. The aorist tenses (received, knew, believed) speak of what happened when they took in Jesus's words.

decisions.choice: I came from you ... you sent me: Jesus's origin with the Father and his mission from him
decisions.reason: Two ways of saying the same truth: Jesus came out from the Father, and the Father sent him. The disciples said just this at 16:30 ("we believe that you came from God"), and Jesus answered it at 16:27-28. The "you" in "you sent me" is emphatic: it was the Father, and no other, who sent him. Believing that the Father sent him is what the Gospel asks of everyone (11:42; 17:21; 20:31).

decisions.choice: For I have passed on to them ... it was you who sent me (B); This is because ... you are the one who sent me (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the verb first and breaks the long sentence in two. Literal brackets [them], which the Greek leaves understood after "received"; the other levels supply it. Readable says "This is because" to tie the sentence to verse 7 (meaning decision m1) and uses the present "know" and "believe" for knowing and faith that last. Balanced and Readable show the emphatic "you" (meaning decision m4), as 11:42 does.

decisions.choice: las palabras ... se las he dado, [las] (L); les he transmitido las palabras ... fuiste tú quien me envió (B); Esto es porque (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Literal keeps the Greek order and brackets the object left understood after "received"; Balanced puts the verb first and splits the sentence; Readable ties the sentence to verse 7 (meaning decision m1). "Fuiste tú quien" shows the emphatic "you", as at 11:42 (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: je suis sorti (L); je suis venu d’auprès de toi (B); je viens de toi (R)
alternatives: je suis sorti de toi (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 16:27-30: Literal keeps the picture of "coming out"; Balanced and Readable use "venir de", which is how French says where someone comes from (meaning decision m4).
